symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1286: on Windows the first `run --local` / `test --local` for a new Mendix version fails with `linking runtime into mxbuild cache: symlink <home>\.mxcli\runtime\11.12.5\runtime <home>\.mxcli\mxbuild\11.12.5\runtime: A required privilege is not held by the client.`; hand-made `New-Item -ItemType Junction` links let the run proceed
cause: ensureMxBuildRuntimeSibling and ensurePADFiles linked a directory with os.Symlink; on Windows CreateSymbolicLink needs SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege (Developer Mode or an elevated token), which an ordinary user lacks (ERROR_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD, 1314). A directory junction needs no privilege
fix: build-tagged linkDir(target, link): POSIX = os.Symlink; Windows = os.Symlink first, and only on errors.Is(err, syscall.Errno(1314)) fall back to `cmd /c mklink /J` (HideWindow, absolute target), returning mklink's output plus the original symlink error if that fails too. mklink rather than FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT keeps golang.org/x/sys an indirect dependency
insight: Linux CI cannot see this: os.Symlink always works there, and a Windows CI runner or a Developer-Mode machine passes too, so the bug only shows on an ordinary Windows user account. The repo's own TestEnsureMxBuildRuntimeSibling already failed on such a machine (the #897 family: Windows-only failures nobody saw) - when a package has long-standing 'pre-existing' Windows failures, read their messages for a privilege/OS cause before writing them off. Safety property to test, not assume: download.go and build.go os.RemoveAll the mxbuild/runtime cache dirs that now contain a junction; Go (1.23+) reports a junction as ModeIrregular (a symlink is ModeSymlink) and RemoveAll deletes the junction itself, not the runtime behind it - measured with go1.26.6 on Windows, target file intact. The test's temp dir has a space in its name because mklink goes through cmd.exe quoting. Wrong turn to skip: do not touch the os.Symlink calls in check_copy.go / marketplace/refcache.go, they recreate existing symlinks while copying trees (a different concern)
test: `cmd/mxcli/docker/linkdir_test.go` (read through link, Stat follows, RemoveAll removes link not target, existing link path errors, Windows fallback proven when os.Symlink returns 1314 and the link is ModeIrregular); `TestEnsureMxBuildRuntimeSibling` now passes on Windows
